[[File:Guy Kargl portrait.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Guy Kargl.]]
'''Guy Kargl''' won Decipher's 1997 Design a Card contest. His design became the [[Special Edition]] Effect [[S-foils]]. He was a 28-year-old hardware and software design engineer and a sanctioned tournament director from Tulsa, Oklahoma.<ref name="linkedin-kargl">[https://www.linkedin.com/in/guy-kargl-eet-pmp-67a2835/ Guy Kargl, EET, PMP], LinkedIn profile, 1 November 2026 (Experience: "Senior Design Engineer, XETA Technologies, Inc, May 1993 – Jul 2006", Broken Arrow, OK; "Assisted in creating a telephone switch (also known as a PBX) system"; "Designed Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs)"; "Wrote Software in Dataflex, HTML, and C"). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261101104014/https://swccg.com/snapshots/linkedin/guy-kargl.html Internet Archive]</ref> He had played the [[Star Wars CCG]] since its November 1995 launch.<ref name="win">[http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/designawinner.html Guy Kargl Wins Star Wars CCG Card Design Contest], Rich Loftus, Decipher (23 May 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990210055006/http://www.decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/designawinner.html Internet Archive]</ref> He was Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]] Red 61 FL from Tulsa. His slot was marked Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.<ref name="smlist" /> He was a call-in guest on [[Radio Free Decipher]] broadcast 9 (26 February 1999) with Chris Swearingen, [[Alex Alcalde]] and [[Carl Mike Hardy|Mike Hardy]].<ref name="rfd-09">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QU24jFxZsHM Radio Free Decipher 09], Player's Council (26 February 1999). Guests Chris Swearingen, [[Alex Alcalde]], Mike Hardy, and [[Guy Kargl]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-QU24jFxZsHM Internet Archive].</ref>
